brief_bullets: Kolkata Police issue 11-point advisory; CM Adhikari hints at scrapping VIP entries at major pandals Among the 19 dead are 13 females, including two minors; the two other deceased minors are males Kolkata’s Bonedi Bari Durga pujas bring together grand colonial-era architecture, family legacies and heirloom recipes.

While the city’s pandals draw the biggest crowds, these ancestral homes offer a more intimate glimpse of the festival, following family traditions dating back more than 300 years Durga Puja celebrations mean glitzy pandals, excessive lighting, high-decibel music and many more attractions.But several committees organising the annual Durga Puja in Kokrajhar town in western Assam, the district headquarters of the Bodoland Territorial Region (BTR), have pitched in to adopt the concept of “carbon-neutral” celebrations by planting trees, reducing the use of non-biodegradable items and even lowering the volume of music systems to check sound pollution.A set of dos and don'ts were proposed by the Kokrajhar district administration for nearly 200 Durga Puja committees in the town as part of efforts to popularise the concept of “carbon-neutral” celebrations.“We proposed the idea as part of our efforts to have environmentally responsible festivities while preserving the religious and cultural essence of the festival.

It is very nice to see that nearly 50 per cent of the committees have responded very positively by significantly reducing the use of plastic items, planting trees and even controlling the volume of music systems,” Kokrajhar District Commissioner Pankaj Chakravarty told DH over the phone on Sunday.

Kokrajhar is situated about 200 km west of Guwahati.Durga Puja celebrations began on Friday and will continue till Wednesday, following which the Durga idols will be immersed in rivers.With a population of nearly 35,000 (2011 Census), Kokrajhar Municipal town has diverse communities, including Bodos, Bengalis, Assamese, Rabhas, Nepalis, Adivasis, Saranias and others, each peacefully celebrating their own festivals.Lotus theme, red-and-white decor to mark Durga Puja in BengaluruCarbon-neutral celebrationsUnder the concept of “carbon-neutral” celebrations, the district administration proposed several measures, such as encouraging the use of locally available and reusable materials, including bamboo, jute, recycled paper and other environmentally responsible alternatives, for pandals and decorations; promoting idols made from natural clay and other biodegradable materials, with non-toxic colours, to minimise environmental pollution, particularly during immersion; tree plantation; the use of solar energy and LED lights; responsible sound management; and encouraging waste segregation, responsible disposal and recycling, among other measures.“This is an encouraging beginning.
The drive is resulting in public awareness, with the concept being shared by many on social media platforms.
why_it_matters_bullets: Shifts federal policy priorities and legislative momentum ahead of upcoming electoral and administrative deadlines.

sources.headline: Tensions flare again in Paris as France counts cost of worst unrest in years - Reuters
France wakes up to one of its worst bouts of unrest in years; one dead, 500 cops injured
France counts cost of worst unrest in years - ThePrint

brief_bullets: Paris: France woke on Sunday to the wreckage of one of its most violent days of unrest in years after protests over high prices and public services left one demonstrator dead, hundreds of police injured and nearly 1,800 people arrested.Nationwide demonstrations erupted into riots on Saturday, with a town hall torched, shops ransacked, and buildings covered in graffiti as violent groups clashed with police in cities across the country.One protester died after suffering a cardiac arrest during demonstrations in Paris, where police made a record 855 arrests.

Across France, police detained some 1,800 people and more than 500 officers were injured, the interior minister said.More than half a million people joined marches in scores of cities, marking the convergence of a month-long student movement with broader social discontent against rising living costs and declining public services.While hundreds of thousands protested peacefully, violent fringe groups targeted public buildings, looted luxury boutiques and supermarkets and attacked police vehicles and officers."No room for violence in our Republic," President Emmanuel Macron posted on X as the unrest unfolded late on Saturday. "Those who have ransacked, attacked the prefectures as well as businesses, looted even our town halls, will be prosecuted and punished."Aucune place pour la violence dans notre République.Ceux qui ont cassé, attaqué les préfectures comme les commerces, pillé jusqu’à nos mairies, seront poursuivis et punis.Aux forces de l’ordre, garantes du droit à manifester, je dis le soutien de la Nation.Nous ferons tous…— Emmanuel Macron (@EmmanuelMacron) October 17, 2026 A massive clean-up operation began in cities from Lille in the north to Marseille in the south and Strasbourg in the east to Bordeaux in the southwest, where a masked mob invaded the residence of the local prefect.Unrest mars day of violent protest in France, as student movement turns nationalIn Paris, smashed shop windows, burnt-out bicycles and spray-painted slogans bore witness to a day that began largely with peaceful demonstrations but descended into violence.In Limoges, workers assessed the damage to the 143-year-old city hall, which was partially destroyed in an arson attack.The unrest has increased pressure on Macron and his government.

Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu said the government would not be "intimidated" by violence, and blamed the unrest on the "ultra-left" and criminals, with a presidential election due next year.Economy Minister Roland Lescure pledged support for business owners who suffered losses. "Those who break things will pay, repair the damage and be held accountable for their intention to sow chaos," Lescure said in a statement.Bordeaux Mayor Thomas Cazenave said up to 100 stores had been looted in his city, while Marseille Mayor Benoit Payan announced emergency financial aid to support those businesses impacted by the violence.The protests began last month over school conditions and teacher shortages in working-class suburbs, before broadening into a movement against inequality, public spending cuts and the rising cost of living.
France counts cost of worst unrest in years ThePrint.
why_it_matters_bullets: Shifts federal policy priorities and legislative momentum ahead of upcoming electoral and administrative deadlines.

stories.primary_headline: Army officer’s wife booked in Jammu & Kashmir over alleged links with Chinese intelligence operatives

primary_source.headline: Army officer’s wife booked in Jammu & Kashmir over alleged links with Chinese intelligence operatives
primary_source.content: Srinagar: Jammu and Kashmir Police have booked the wife of a serving Army officer for alleged espionage-related activities involving foreign intelligence operatives, including those linked to China, with investigators examining research papers she allegedly prepared on sensitive defence and geopolitical issues.The woman, a freelance researcher from Telangana, has not been arrested, and a preliminary inquiry has not established that she shared sensitive information, official sources said on Sunday.The case was registered at Gandhi Nagar police station on Friday under the Official Secrets Act, 1923, and relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).She was questioned by a Deputy Superintendent of Police-rank officer following the registration of the FIR, according to a PTI report.'Espionage Alert': UK accuses China of using academics to spy on AI and other tech researchInvestigators are examining allegations that the woman was tasked with preparing analytical papers on subjects including Line of Control (LoC) dynamics in Jammu and Kashmir, critical infrastructure projects in Arunachal Pradesh and drone deployment, sources said.The assignments allegedly involved individuals linked to Chinese intelligence operatives, they said.According to reports, the woman is well-qualified, undertook an IT internship with the United Nations in 2023 and currently works as a freelance researcher.The investigation is seeking to establish the nature of her contacts with foreign entities and whether any information or material was communicated to them.The allegations have not been independently established, and police have not publicly detailed the evidence recovered or confirmed whether any classified documents were involved.The investigation comes months after a Delhi court acquitted five accused in a separate espionage case registered in 2015.The accused, including serving and former security personnel, had faced charges under the Official Secrets Act over allegations of passing information about Army and Border Security Force deployments in Jammu and Kashmir to Pakistan-based intelligence operatives.In its May 20, 2026, judgment, the court found that the prosecution had failed to establish that the documents allegedly recovered were classified official records and that protected information had been communicated to enemy agents. All five accused were acquitted.

primary_source.headline: Anti-CEC stir | Delhi Police registers cases, arrests 5 persons over attacks on protesters
primary_source.content: New Delhi: Delhi Police has registered at least 10 FIRs and arrested five people in connection with alleged harassment and assaults on protesters demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, with several social media posts accusing right-wing activists of targeting demonstrators, officials said on Sunday.The cases were registered between October 11 and 14 at Connaught Place and Kamla Market police stations after videos and posts highlighting alleged attacks on protesters circulated on social media.At least five people have been arrested in two separate cases, a senior police officer said.According to the police, an FIR was registered at Connaught Place police station on October 13 in connection with an incident flagged through social media handles.Delhi Police registers four FIRs against 'rumour-mongers', Pak social media handles under scannerGaurav was arrested in the case, while efforts are underway to trace his alleged accomplices.A group of men was seen assaulting a protester while daring others to call them "cockroaches". One of the men was also heard threatening to beat up anyone who spoke against the prime minister or the police.In another case, registered at Kamla Market police station on October 11, four people were arrested after a video purportedly showing individuals harassing and assaulting protesters went viral.Police took suo motu cognisance of the incident and initiated legal action against those allegedly involved.The list of cases also includes multiple FIRs registered at Connaught Place police station on October 13 and 14 over incidents highlighted in social media posts and videos. Police are examining CCTV footage to identify those involved, establish the sequence of events and determine the roles of the suspected accused.EC-SIR row: Delhi Police take down 300 social media for spreading 'rumours'Several social media posts have alleged that right-wing activists assaulted or harassed protesters during the demonstrations.The footage and allegations are being examined by police as they work to identify the people involved and establish the circumstances surrounding the incidents.The police action comes amid a wider scrutiny of online content related to the protests, with authorities also investigating posts allegedly circulating misinformation, rumours and fabricated videos.Some social media accounts have shared claims of police brutality against demonstrators, which investigators are examining to establish their authenticity.In one of the cases, police have sought information from social media platform X to identify a user accused of uploading videos that they suspect were fabricated and circulated to disrupt public order.Police have identified more than 37 social media accounts, including over 17 allegedly linked to right-wing groups, for purportedly circulating misleading content related to the protests, a source in the police said.Takedown notices have been issued to more than 17 handles, including those linked to right-wing groups, and action has been initiated under relevant provisions of the Information Technology Act and other laws for allegedly inciting people and disrupting law and order, they said.Some right-wing accounts allegedly shared posts and reels targeting protesters and presenting the demonstrations in a misleading manner, while other users circulated videos purportedly showing police brutality against demonstrators.Investigators are examining the content to verify its authenticity and identify those responsible, the officials added.The protests in the national capital have been organised over demands for Kumar's resignation and a rollback of the SIR exercise. Further investigation in the cases is underway.

One of the men was also heard threatening to beat up anyone who spoke against the prime minister or the police.In another case, registered at Kamla Market police station on October 11, four people were arrested after a video purportedly showing individuals harassing and assaulting protesters went viral.Police took suo motu cognisance of the incident and initiated legal action against those allegedly involved.The list of cases also includes multiple FIRs registered at Connaught Place police station on October 13 and 14 over incidents highlighted in social media posts and videos.

Police are examining CCTV footage to identify those involved, establish the sequence of events and determine the roles of the suspected accused.EC-SIR row: Delhi Police take down 300 social media for spreading 'rumours'Several social media posts have alleged that right-wing activists assaulted or harassed protesters during the demonstrations.The footage and allegations are being examined by police as they work to identify the people involved and establish the circumstances surrounding the incidents.The police action comes amid a wider scrutiny of online content related to the protests, with authorities also investigating posts allegedly circulating misinformation, rumours and fabricated videos.Some social media accounts have shared claims of police brutality against demonstrators, which investigators are examining to establish their authenticity.In one of the cases, police have sought information from social media platform X to identify a user accused of uploading videos that they suspect were fabricated and circulated to disrupt public order.Police have identified more than 37 social media accounts, including over 17 allegedly linked to right-wing groups, for purportedly circulating misleading content related to the protests, a source in the police said.Takedown notices have been issued to more than 17 handles, including those linked to right-wing groups, and action has been initiated under relevant provisions of the Information Technology Act and other laws for allegedly inciting people and disrupting law and order, they said.Some right-wing accounts allegedly shared posts and reels targeting protesters and presenting the demonstrations in a misleading manner, while other users circulated videos purportedly showing police brutality against demonstrators.Investigators are examining the content to verify its authenticity and identify those responsible, the officials added.The protests in the national capital have been organised over demands for Kumar's resignation and a rollback of the SIR exercise.
Further investigation in the cases is underway.
